nodes.name: business_tool_registry.py is a read-only external-tool recommendation catalog, not the internal execution Tool Registry

source_of_truth.scope: which external (third-party) business tools are approved/verified for recommendation to a user, and the deterministic metadata (categories, capabilities, when-to-use) used to select among them. The runtime-visible tool set is sourced from a generated snapshot (data/tool_registry/runtime_snapshot.json) rather than solely from business_tool_registry.py's own hand-curated Python data -- see precedence.
source_of_truth.precedence: tool_registry.py remains the sole canonical authority for the internal execution Tool Registry (roles_allowed/tenant_scoped/requires_approval/dispatch eligibility); business_tool_registry.py has no precedence over it and cannot be extended to originate one. business_tool_registry.py's list_tools()/maybe_recommend() now read data/tool_registry/runtime_snapshot.json (via tools/tool_runtime_snapshot.py's load_tool_runtime_snapshot()) as their live data source when the snapshot loads successfully; business_tool_registry.py's inline _PLAYBOOKS dict is enrichment data only (playbook steps), not the tool list itself. The snapshot is itself generated offline from a Postgres-backed editorial catalog (core/migrations/002_tool_catalog.sql's tools/capabilities tables, populated via tools/tool_catalog_db.py/tools/import_tool_catalog_seed.py, exported via tools/generate_tool_runtime_snapshot_from_db.py) -- this DB is editorial/offline state only, per its own module docstrings ('Runtime never calls this module; it reads the validated local snapshot produced here'); nothing in the live request path (app.py, dispatcher, ActionGateway) queries Postgres for this data directly. This decision node's original precedence claim (business_tool_registry.py has no precedence over tool_registry.py / cannot grant execution authority) is UNCHANGED by this update -- the DB-backed pipeline only changes how the external-recommendation catalog's *content* is authored/generated, not what it is permitted to do.

notes: Registered to resolve a Context Librarian REVIEW_REQUIRED finding: business_tool_registry.py is a static, hand-curated dataclass catalog of external SCOREBOS tools consumed by app.py's maybe_recommend() early in the inbound-message flow (before router/dispatcher), to suggest tools to the user in conversation.

Explicit boundary, matching the EXTERNAL_RECOMMENDATION_CATALOG policy: this module is NOT the internal execution Tool Registry, cannot dispatch or execute a business action, and cannot grant ActionGateway/tool execution authority. tool_registry.py remains the internal execution registry for every dispatcher-routed tool.

No existing catalog layer covers this scope (layer.tools' code_paths are the internal dispatcher-tool implementations under tools/) — this decision creates a narrow boundary for the external-recommendation concept rather than folding the file into layer.tools' internal-execution scope.

OWNER DECISION (PR #651, owner-decision-queue resolution): 6 files from a same-day 'SCOREBOS Tool Catalog Phase 2' effort (commits 5d469fe/3f63d7e/c8f484e/47f66bd/5db33a7/fa35284, all 14/08/2026, none authored by this session) registered here rather than as a new decision node -- owner explicitly confirmed this is the same governed external-recommendation-catalog decision class, with a new editorial/generation implementation behind it, not a new authority boundary, and it does not get a separate decision node; tool_registry.py remains the separate internal execution authority. Basis (direct code read, not a guess): business_tool_registry.py:269 calls tools.tool_runtime_snapshot.load_tool_runtime_snapshot(), and app.py's maybe_recommend() call site is unchanged. confidence restored to 0.85 (matching the sibling business_tool_registry.py registration) following owner confirmation of this framing. NOT verified, and not claimed: whether core/migrations/002_tool_catalog.sql's migration has actually been applied against any real (staging/production) Postgres instance, or is only exercised via the CI Postgres service in test_tool_catalog_db.py -- this registration makes no production-deployment-state claim.

context_librarian.registration.purpose: curated, read-only catalog of approved external tools and their recommendation metadata, consumed by app.py's maybe_recommend() to suggest (never execute) a tool to the user
